title: update and the pointer grammar
description: User story under REQ-173. Every ledger supports `update <id>` with field patches validated as `add` validates; `resolvedBy` on a brief statement is a closed pointer grammar validated by D2.
iWant: to patch a statement's kind, text or resolution
soThat: a correction does not mint a duplicate

acceptanceCriteria.description: [happy] given statement 7, when rcf define ledger brief update 7 --kind constraint --resolved-by REQ-003 runs, then the statement carries kind constraint and resolvedBy REQ-003 and its id and addedAt are unchanged.
[happy] given decision 2 with one option, when rcf define ledger decisions update 2 --option a:x --option b:y --default a runs, then decisions:wellFormed passes it.

[happy] given each pointer form REQ-nnn, TAD.entity:<name>, PRD.user:<name>, TAD.system:<name>, TAC-nnnn and omitted:<reason> resolving on the fixture, when D2 runs, then skeleton:resolvedBy passes the statement.
[failure] given --resolved-by "loan thing", when update runs, then it exits 2 naming the grammar and writes nothing.
[failure] given --resolved-by REQ-999 on a tree with no REQ-999, when D2 runs, then skeleton:resolvedBy fails the statement with "pointer does not resolve".
[must-not] given a statement whose text contains an existing REQ title and no resolvedBy, when D2 runs in 0.30.0, then skeleton:resolvedBy does not pass it on the title hit.

[happy] (R1 2026-10-05) given rcf define ledger brief add --id 3 --text "foo" --kind capability on a ledger whose entry 3 already carries kind capability and text foo, when the verb runs, then it exits 0 and stdout reads 'brief-ledger: unchanged 3' (with --json, {"status":"unchanged","id":3}); the file is not rewritten.

[failure] (R1 2026-10-05) given rcf define ledger brief add --id 3 --text "bar" --kind constraint on a ledger whose entry 3 carries kind capability and text foo, when the verb runs, then it exits 3 and stderr names the id and the differing fields (text, kind); the file is not rewritten.

[happy] (R1 2026-10-05) given rcf define ledger brief add --text "foo" with no --id on an empty ledger, when the verb runs, then it mints id 1 as before (idempotency opt-in is id-carried; the harness threads --id back on replay).

[happy] (R1 create extension 2026-10-05, PR 292 follow-up; amended on the PR 293 landing review) given rcf define create ac --parent US-1 --id AC-1-1 --description "foo" on a tree where US-1 already carries AC-1-1 with description foo and testable true and no other fields, when the verb runs, then it exits 0 and stdout reads 'AC-1-1: unchanged (rcf/user-stories/us-1.json)'; the parent US file is not rewritten; and given the same verb with --description "bar" instead, it exits 3, stderr names the id and the differing field (description), and the file is not rewritten. rcf define create has no --json flag; the stdout line is the whole output (suppressed by --quiet).

[happy] (R1 create extension, PR 293 landing review) given rcf define create tc --parent TS-1 --id TC-1-foo --ac AC-1-1 --description "foo" --test-pointer t.test.js::foo on a tree where TS-1 already carries TC-1-foo with the same acId, description, testPointer and status pending, when the verb runs, then it exits 0 and stdout reads 'TC-1-foo: unchanged (rcf/test-suites/ts-1.json)' and the file is not rewritten; given the same verb with --description "bar", it exits 3 naming the id and the differing field (description) and the file is not rewritten. Idempotency is id-carried: without --id, a derived-slug collision still refuses with exit 2 and the 'supply --slug explicitly' message.

[happy] (R1 create extension, PR 293 landing review) given rcf define create cn --id CN-1 --path src/a.js --acs AC-1-1 on a tree where CN-1 already carries path src/a.js, implementsAcIds [AC-1-1], dependencies [], version 0.1.0 and status draft, when the verb runs, then it exits 0 and stdout reads 'CN-1: unchanged (rcf/code-nodes/cn-1.json)' and the file is not rewritten; given the same verb with --path src/b.js, it exits 3 naming the id and the differing field (path) and the file is not rewritten.

[happy] (R1 create extension, PR 293 landing review) given rcf define create req --parent PRD-001 --id REQ-050 --title T --description D whose first run persisted a classifier-owned shapeClassification block, when the identical command is replayed, then it exits 0 and stdout reads 'REQ-050: unchanged (rcf/requirements/req-050.json)' and the file is not rewritten: the replay compare ignores every writer- and classifier-owned field (createdAt, updatedAt, shapeClassification; one exported REPLAY_IGNORE_FIELDS list in src/core/store/writer.js); given the same verb with a different --description, it exits 3 naming description and the file is not rewritten.
